Maria (support): ACME on Dedicated pool-43 reporting huge throughput drop starting ~10:08 UTC. They say requests are queuing and p99 latency jumped from 120ms -> 2.4s. They also saw some 502/504s. Can eng-runtime please triage?
Sam (eng-runtime): Thanks Maria. Do we have pool id and example request IDs? Any recent deploys to that pool?
Maria (support): Pool ID: pool-43. Customer provided request ids: rQXc9, rQXcA, rQXcG. No deploys on our side; they claim autoscale didn't add nodes.
Sam (eng-runtime): Pulling metrics now. @ops-bot can you dump queue depth / batch size timeseries for pool-43 last 30m?
ops-bot: Metrics export: queue_depth=[2,3,6,18,40,52,58,60], avg_batch_size=[64,60,48,20,6,4], p99_latency_ms=[120,130,500,1200,2400] (30m window).
Sam (eng-runtime): OK looks like a queue sink: queue depth keeps increasing while avg batch size collapses. That suggests the scheduler is waiting for large token-prefill batches but requests are short, so we end up with small underfilled batches and long waits. Also seeing a handful of very long-context requests from tenant acme-analytics that are monopolizing KV cache and filling token budget.
Jon (infra): Autoscaler logs: scale decision uses GPU_util and pending_requests. GPU_util stayed < 40% — autoscaler didn't scale because throughput was gated by batching not saturation. pending_requests threshold not crossed in autoscaler because requests were marked as 'in-flight' while waiting in batcher prefill window.
Eva (oncall): So autoscale logic misinterpreted queued-but-prefilling requests as in-flight -> no scale up. That's a neat race.
ACME Support (customer): Our SREs also saw a flurry of long-run analytics jobs from tenant acme-analytics on the same pool around 10:05. We can throttle them if that helps. Customer is worried about billing impact if we spin up more nodes.
Sam (eng-runtime): Short-term mitigations: 1) throttle acme-analytics (reduce concurrency) 2) reduce batch_timeout_ms from 50 -> 10 for pool-43 to avoid long prefill waits 3) reduce max_batch_tokens from 8192 -> 2048 to prevent single long requests from filling the token budget and stalling small requests.
Jon (infra): I can add 2x warm workers into the pool as an emergency to buy time, but it'll cost them. Recommend deploying the batching param tweaks first.
Maria (support): ACME approved the config changes, prefer we try config tweaks before adding capacity. They asked for repro steps so they can test.
Sam (eng-runtime): Repro steps for SRE: run this traffic mix against pool-43 (from a bastion):
```
# 1) flood with short requests (len ~ 32 tokens)
wrk -t8 -c200 -d60s --lua=short_requests.lua http://pool-43.redux.internal/generate
# 2) concurrently run a few long analytic requests (len ~ 6000 tokens)
wrk -t4 -c8 -d60s --lua=long_requests.lua http://pool-43.redux.internal/generate
```
Observe avg_batch_size and batch_timeout wait times in tracing. If queue depth grows while avg_batch_size drops, that's the same issue.
Sam (eng-runtime): Logged a small code tweak to treat 'prefilling' requests as pending for autoscaler so pending_requests counter is correct: GH#redwood/rt#4582. Will push a canary patch to staging after code review.
Eva (oncall): I've applied batch_timeout_ms=10 and max_batch_tokens=2048 to pool-43. Monitoring now.
ops-bot: Config change detected on pool-43: batch_timeout_ms=10, max_batch_tokens=2048 by Eva at 2026-03-17T10:25:30Z.
Sam (eng-runtime): Early signs: queue depth started dropping and avg_batch_size climbed back to ~48. p95 latency down to 220ms. :thumbsup:
ACME Support (customer): Confirming throughput looks normal on our end now. Thanks. We'll still throttle analytics jobs for the next 24h.
Maria (support): Customer happy for now. Action items: Sam to follow up with autoscaler fix GH#4582, Jon to keep emergency workers on standby, Eva to roll batch defaults to 20ms for pools with mixed tenants. I'll update the ticket and billing note.
Sam (eng-runtime): Will follow up. One more note — schedule a postmortem to look at tenant isolation (noisy neighbor) and whether we should auto-migrate long-context jobs to dedicated pools.
Jon (infra): Agree — noisy neighbor isolation is next.
Maria (support): Closing loop with ACME and adding summary to the incident ticket. :white_check_mark:
